mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (أن أنذر قومك): (أن) has no position in i'rab; it is only for explanation, meaning (أي) "that is". It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by omission of the preposition, i.e. "with: warn". Its like in both aspects is (أن اعبدوا الله).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (ليلا ونهارا): two adverbials of time (ẓarf zamān), and the governor of both is (دعوت).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (إلا فرارا): the second object of (يزدهم).
His saying (وإني كلما): (كلما) is accusative as an adverbial, and its governor is (جعلوا).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (دعوتهم جهارا): (جهارا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being open in calling them". It is also said the implied form is "possessing openness". It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (مدرارا): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (السماء). The hāʾ [of the feminine] was not kept because the pattern mifʿāl for the feminine comes without hāʾ when it runs on the verb, as in (امرأة مذكار) "a woman who bears males", (مئناث) "who bears females" and (مطلاق) "often divorced".
His saying (سموات طباقا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (سبع). Al-Farrāʾ allowed, outside the Qur'an, (طباق) in the genitive as a naʿt of (سموات).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying (نورا) and (سراجا): two objects of (جعل), because it means "made into" (صيّر), so it takes two objects. Its like is (بساطا).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (من الأرض نباتا): (نبات) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of a verb indicated by (أنبتكم), i.e. "so you grew a growing". It is also said that it is the maṣdar of (أنبتكم) with the augment dropped.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying (وولده): whoever reads it with ḍamma on the wāw makes it the plural of (ولد), like (وثن) and (وثن) [Translator's note: i.e. waṯan, pl. wuṯn]. It is also said that it is a dialectal form of the singular: one says (ولد) and (ولد) [i.e. walad and wuld], on the pattern of (بخل) and (بخل) [bakhal and bukhl].

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying (ولا يغوث ويعوق): both are accusative by conjunction with (ود). These are names of idols. (يغوث) and (يعوق) are diptotes because they are on the pattern of (يقوم) and (يقول) [Translator's note: the printed text has «بقوم»] and they are definite. Al-Aʿmash read them as fully declinable, which is far-fetched, as if he made them indefinite; and this has no sense, since not every idol is named Yaghūth and Yaʿūq; they are only the names of two known, specific idols, so there is no reason to make them indefinite.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (مما خطيئاتهم): (ما) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and (خطيئاتهم) is genitive governed by (من).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying (من الكافرين ديارا): it is on the pattern fayʿāl from (دار يدور), i.e. "do not leave on the earth anyone of them who moves about". Its origin is (ديوار); then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, like (ميت), whose origin is (ميوت), and then the second was assimilated into the first. It may also be that they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and then assimilated the first yāʾ into the second. It is not permissible for (ديار) to be on the pattern faʿʿāl, because it would then have to be (دوار), and the word is not so.
